audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows were scored against their own explanation. Levels 2 and 3 read Swain while whys[1] and whys[2] describe you stacking sweetspots on a flat-footed Swain; Level 6 read Skill under a why that literally opens 'Swain's window'; first item read Swain under a why ending 'so it's even'.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill / Lillia / Lillia / Skill / Swain / Skill / Swain, which matches the prose on all four rows. The tokens were wrong, not the writing.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 4 and 5 proposed as matched full+content pairs onto the packet chart, with ratings adjusted to fit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's level 6, first item and 2+ item lines were template text promising guaranteed ganks and melted tanks on stages Swain owns or splits.
audit.why: Level 6 is his spike, not yours — Demonic Ascension sustains through exactly the chip damage Lillia deals, and it persists indefinitely as long as he keeps draining champions, so the counter is leaving, not out-damaging.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten around the root-into-drain sequence and the soul-stack heal race.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important mechanic in this matchup was never stated: Nevermove roots on the RETURN of the wave, not on the way out. The page only says 'if Nevermove lands it roots me'.
audit.why: A Lillia who sidesteps the outgoing wave and then keeps kiting in a straight line walks into the return and gets rooted anyway — which is the whole loss condition of the lane. Also unstated: Vision of Empire grants him a Soul Fragment whenever it clips a champion, so eating his W permanently raises his max health.
audit.corrected: The return-root added to report[5].t and early with the 850 range and 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s cooldown; the Soul Fragment consequence and the Grievous Wounds requirement added to late.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d invited you in for a 'fifteen-second invitation' after he burns Demonic Ascension.
audit.why: Riot's text gives no duration — the form is indefinite while he drains champions — so fifteen seconds is invented. The real punishable cooldown is Nevermove at 12s, since without the root he cannot start anything.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the Nevermove number; dosFull[0].d rewritten to say his ult ends when you walk away from it.

edits.before: Swain is an immobile mage who has to walk into Q range to farm, so levels 1-3 I lean on what kites him: Blooming Blows sweetspots stack my move speed while the outer-edge hit chips, and an E Swirlseed slow pins him flat so the Dream Dust burn starts ticking. The one thing that ruins my day is his E pull — if Nevermove lands it roots me and the whole W-bomb-Q-poke rotation lands on a body that can't run, and I have no defensive button. So I poke from the edge, never hug the wave inside his E range, and respect that his Q out-ranges my short hops.
edits.after: Swain is an immobile mage who has to walk into Q range to farm, so levels 1-3 lean on what kites him: Blooming Blows sweetspots stack your move speed while the outer edge chips, and a Swirlseed slow pins him flat so the Dream Dust burn starts ticking. The button that ruins your day is Nevermove, and it roots on the way BACK, not on the way out — sidestepping the outgoing wave is only half the dodge, so clear the return path too. Rooted, you eat the whole W-bomb and Q rotation with no defensive button. Poke from the edge and stay outside its 850 range.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are my best lane window on paper — full Q rank, the DoT compounding, and enough mana to grind down anyone who has to walk at me, which Swain does. I chip him while my move speed keeps me out of pull range. But level 6 hands him the swing: his E pull-into-root catches me mid-kite, and once he pops R Demonic Ascension the sustained AOE drain plus a W bomb out-heals my hit-and-run chip in any fight I can't immediately leave. My own R is a delayed sleep, not a duel button, so I don't try to solo his ult — I bait the E, kite the root cooldown, and only commit my sleep with a jungler.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your best lane window — full Q rank, the DoT compounding, and a Swain who has to walk at you. Chip him while your move speed keeps you outside Nevermove's 850 range. Level 6 hands him the swing: the root catches you mid-kite, and once Demonic Ascension is up the drain plus a W bomb out-heals your chip in any fight you cannot immediately leave. His ult persists only while he keeps draining champions, so the answer is distance, not damage. Your R is a delayed sleep, not a duel button — bait the E, count its 12s, and commit with a jungler.

edits.before: This tilts to Swain late and I have to be honest about it. A full-build Swain is a permanent R drain machine — the moment his E pulls and roots me even once, his soul-stacked heal eats my entire Dream Dust DoT and I can't hit-and-run my way back out. My W and Liandry's/Riftmaker percent-HP burn keep me relevant in the scramble, but a straight extended fight is his. So I stop trying to win the sidelane duel: I use my move speed to roam and skirmish, isolate-sleep him with R only when my team can follow up, and let the burn matter in a 5v5 where I'm never the one standing in his drain.
edits.after: This tilts to Swain late. A full-build Swain is a permanent drain machine — the moment Nevermove roots you once, his soul-stacked healing eats your entire Dream Dust DoT and there is no hit-and-run back out. Grievous Wounds is not optional on your team, and every Vision of Empire that clips a champion hands him another Soul Fragment and permanent max health, so dodging the eye is worth more than the damage it deals. Liandry's keeps you relevant in a scramble, but a long fight is his. Roam on your move speed, sleep him only when your team follows up, and never stand in the drain.

notes: Death's Hand bolts pierce and stack damage per bolt that hits, so walking at Swain head-on through a thin wave eats several at once — real, but it needs more length than any single field had spare, so I left it out rather than push a string past the band. Flagging it as a candidate if the user ever wants one field expanded.
